definitions.explanation: A sticky Japanese rice cake made from glutinous rice that has been pounded into a paste.

examples.japanese: {正月|しょうがつ}に{餅|もち}を{食|た}べる。
examples.english: We eat mochi at New Year's.

examples.japanese: {餅|もち}をつく{音|おと}が{聞|き}こえる。
examples.english: I can hear the sound of pounding mochi.

examples.japanese: {餅|もち}は{喉|のど}に{詰|つ}まりやすいので{気|き}をつけて。
examples.english: Be careful because mochi can easily get stuck in your throat.

notes:
{餅|もち} is a traditional Japanese food made from glutinous rice ({餅米|もちごめ}) that is steamed and pounded.

COMMON TYPES:
- お{雑煮|ぞうに} (mochi soup eaten at New Year's)
- {草餅|くさもち} (mugwort mochi)
- {大福|だいふく} (mochi filled with sweet bean paste)
- {切|き}り{餅|もち} (pre-cut mochi squares)

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {餅|もち}をつく (to pound mochi)
- {餅|もち}を{焼|や}く (to grill/toast mochi)
- {餅|もち}が{伸|の}びる (mochi stretches)

SAFETY NOTE:
Every year in Japan, people (especially elderly) choke on mochi. It should be eaten carefully, in small pieces.
